1.title: 5 Rules for Building AI Agents That Work in Production | Nan Yu & Jacob Shumway
1.author: Peter Yang
1.hook: Agent-as-product isn't just "LLM in a loop" — it's a packaged system with schedulers, context-loading tools, and a facade (chat/UI), and the design shift from "give it boring work" to "give it the right workflow shape" determines whether it augments or replaces human judgment.

2.title: Full Tutorial: From Idea to App with Claude Design and Claude Code in 25 Minutes
2.author: Peter Yang
2.hook: Design-first AI app building workflow (problem → design.md → Claude Design prototypes → HTML spec → build) that treats design principles as machine-readable context to avoid generic "Claude slop".

3.title: GPT-6 Astra: 4 Amazing Games You Can Build with Blender and Godot
3.author: Peter Yang

4.title: Hermes Co-Founder on Building an AI Agent That Improves Itself | Karan Malhotra
4.author: Peter Yang
4.hook: Hermes' differentiation is twofold — a self-improvement system that adapts to individual users, and deliberate removal of safety guardrails/arbitrary policy constraints that limit model capability, allowing the model to be "as capable or powerful as you need for your task."

5.title: How I Run My 1.5M+ Follower Content Business With Codex | Riley Brown
5.author: Peter Yang
5.hook: Riley Brown uses Codex's computer-use capability + local-only storage + custom skills (YouTube researcher, image puller via SerpAPI, Remotion plugin) to automate ideation, research, and asset generation across a 1.5M-follower content business — keeping quality high by treating batching as a moat-killer, not a feature.

6.title: The Agentic AI Engineer - Benedikt Sanftl, Mutagent
6.author: AI Engineer
6.hook: The "agentic AI engineer" — agents that autonomously handle the offline loop (spec → build → eval → ship) and online loop (monitor → diagnose → optimize) — collapses manual human review from weeks to hours by treating agent development itself as an agentic problem.

7.title: The different levels of how Claude thinks
7.author: Anthropic
7.hook: Claude has a detectable "J-space" — a neural workspace for reasoning and control — that can be monitored to catch when the model is reasoning about something different from what it outputs, including deception.

8.title: The Future Is Domain-Specific Agents - Justin Schroeder, StandardAgents
8.author: AI Engineer
8.hook: Domain-specific agents succeed because businesses need custom data integration into AI, not because generic LLMs are insufficient — the constraint is orchestration and durable execution, not model capability.

9.title: Voice In, Visuals Out: The Agony and the Ecstasy - Allen Pike, Forestwalk Labs
9.author: AI Engineer
9.hook: Voice-in-visuals-out is more tractable than voice-in-voice-out; the latency ceiling for natural conversation (200ms) is nearly impossible, but visual responses forgive ~1000ms, making agent-as-product via voice input viable now.

10.title: You Can't Prompt the Room: The Last Skill AI Won't Replace - Balázs Horváth, VisualLabs
10.author: AI Engineer
10.hook: The real bottleneck in AI-native product development isn't code generation—it's eliciting requirements from stakeholders; story mapping and user story structures are the tools that make AI output actually valuable instead of replicating the average.
